page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.14xlarge is an x86_64 virtualization instance belonging to the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 56 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6149 processor running at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. System memory totals 160.0 GB, which translates to a memory density of 2.86 GB per core. The server does not incorporate hardware GPU accelerators.

Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 10 Gbps, providing reliable inter-node communication for scaled architectures. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring persistence and system disks to be provisioned via external cloud storage services. Furthermore, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly to the instance, requiring explicit configuration for public internet access.

From an efficiency perspective, the provision of 56 dedicated cores operating at 3.1 GHz offers strong parallel compute capacity and thread execution stability. The 2.86 GB per vCPU ratio makes it cost-efficient for compute-dominated workloads that do not require massive memory buffers. Architectural tradeoffs include the lack of local scratch disks and reliance on network-attached storage, which shifts disk I/O performance entirely to remote storage configurations.

Workloads aligned with the ecs.hfg5.14xlarge profile include distributed batch processing, continuous integration build clusters, front-end web application scaling tiers, video encoding, and compute-intensive enterprise applications requiring high core counts.

It is well matched for distributed compilation, high-throughput web serving, parallel batch tasks, and CPU-bound enterprise software suites.
